steps.text: Olive the owl was very proud of her night-eyes and her silent wings.
She usually stayed in her glowing grove, calling herself the Queen of the Quiet.
But one sunny morning, curiosity pulled her onto the winding dirt path.
The world was loud! The sunlight filtered through the leaves in dancing patches of gold.
A sudden rush of wind whistled past her ears.
Olive fluttered her wings, feeling very small in the big, bright day.

steps.text: At the brook, the water sang a song over the flat stepping stones.
Pip the rabbit was there, splashing in the shallows with Sammy the squirrel.
Olive watched them from a distance. She saw Pip share a piece of sweet clover with Sammy.
The two friends bumped shoulders and giggled.
Olive felt a strange prickle in her chest.
'It is very fine to be alone,' Olive told herself. 'But it is very warm to be together.'

steps.text: In the wide, sunny clearing, they met Ruby the robin, who was singing a melody of summer.
Olive stood at the edge of the grass, her feathers ruffled.
She felt like a grey smudge in a world of bright colors.
She almost flew back to her silent grove to be the Queen of the Quiet again.
But then, Ruby flew over and landed just a few inches from Olive's talons.
'You have the most beautiful eyes I have ever seen,' Ruby sang.
Olive blinked. No one had ever said that to her before.
The group gathered at the great mossy stump to share a feast of berries and seeds.
Olive found that she liked the noise. She liked the way Sammy told jokes and the way Pip listened.
For the first time, Olive didn't mind being the only owl in the circle.
She realized that being brave enough to be alone was good, but being brave enough to ask for company was even better.
'Will you stay with us?' Pip asked. 'Just until the stars come out?'
'I think,' Olive whispered, 'I would like that very much.'
As the sun dipped low, the woods began to change.
Soft blue mushrooms lit the path like tiny lanterns. This was Olive's favorite time.
She showed her friends the way through the glowing grove, leading them with a proud flutter of her wings.
The others watched in wonder as the forest turned silver and teal.
Olive wasn't just the Queen of the Quiet anymore. She was a guide.
At the fork in the night path, the air was filled with magic.
Hundreds of fireflies drifted around them, swirling like slow, warm snow.
Olive danced in the middle of the lights, her laughter mixing with the chirps of her new friends.
The dark was no longer just a place to be alone. It was a place to share.
Under the glowing moon, the friends found a soft patch of moss to call their own.
The forest was returning to its quiet, but it was a warm, shared quiet now.
Sammy curled his bushy tail around his nose.
Pip tucked his long ears down tight.
Ruby rested her small head beneath a wing.
And Olive, the Queen of the Quiet, closed her eyes, feeling the heartbeat of her friends beside her.
The moon watched over them, silver and still.
Goodnight, Olive. Goodnight, little friends.
Goodnight.
